react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome is dominated by perturbation of xenobiotic metabolism. Across three independent paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA (Reactome namespace), Mummichog m/z-direct enrichment (human_mfn network), and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — the top convergent finding is Xenobiotics metabolism. In RaMP, REACT:R-HSA-211981 ranks 4th with FDR=0.0072 (coumarin as the sole hit, 1 of 52 pathway members), and its parent Reactome 'Xenobiotics' super-pathway (R-HSA-211897) for cytochrome P450 substrates is also significant at FDR=0.009. Mummichog independently recovers 'Xenobiotics metabolism' (MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism) as its rank-0 hit (p=0.003) with two overlapping compounds. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA identifies KEGG:hsa00350 at rank 0 (p=0.052, gentisic acid hit), which encompasses aromatic xenobiotic catabolism. Coumarin (ChEBI:28794) is the primary driver: it is the sole input metabolite recovered in the xenobiotics pathway in both RaMP and Mummichog, and its InChIKey (ZYGHJZDHTFUPRJ) is structurally consistent across all compound references. Benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (BaP DE, ChEBI:30614) is the Phase I activation product of the carcinogen benzo[a]pyrene via cytochrome P450 enzymes — consistent with the RaMP cytochrome P450 pathway hit — placing it upstream of DNA-adduct formation. A secondary convergent signal is iron homeostasis: RaMP identifies 'Iron uptake and transport' (R-HSA-917937, FDR=0.007) and 'Metal sequestration by antimicrobial proteins' (R-HSA-6799990, FDR=0.006), both with gentisic acid (2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid, ChEBI:17189) as the hit, suggesting altered systemic iron handling. Mummichog independently recovers ubiquinone biosynthesis (rank 2, p=0.022), a pathway that requires iron as a cofactor for several enzymes. The metabolite set thus reflects a dual insult: xenobiotic Phase I/II processing stress (coumarin + BaP DE) and iron homeostasis perturbation (gentisic acid + elemental iron).

use run_ramp_enrichment (multi-DB ORA, broader namespace coverage) or run_metaboanalystr_psea (KEGG-specific ORA) instead

pathway_members.sqlite only indexes HUMAN1 + RECON2; for namespace 'REACT', inspect the `metabolites_hit` list inside an EnrichmentResult (e.g. from run_ramp_enrichment) — it carries the method-specific compound roster

try search_literature for biological context, or reconcile_inchikey if you have multiple ID variants

react_result.final_narrative_text: Cross-paradigm analysis of the seven differentially abundant metabolites identified two dominant biological themes. The first is xenobiotic metabolism: Mummichog places Xenobiotics metabolism (MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism) as its top hit with p=0.0042, and RaMP independently recovers the Reactome Xenobiotics pathway (REACT:R-HSA-211981) at rank 4 with FDR=0.0072. Coumarin (KEGG:C05851, ChEBI:28794) is the sole hit in both pathway hits, confirmed by the metabolites_hit field. The second theme is iron homeostasis perturbation: RaMP places Iron uptake and transport (REACT:R-HSA-917937, FDR=0.0072, rank 1) and Metal sequestration by antimicrobial proteins (REACT:R-HSA-6799990, FDR=0.0060, rank 0) as its two highest-ranking hits. Both pathways are driven by gentisic acid (2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid; KEGG:C00628, ChEBI:17189), the only input metabolite resolved by the enrichment pipeline for these two pathways. MetaboAnalystR independently recovers KEGG:hsa00350 as its sole hit at p=0.0521 with gentisic acid as the sole overlap. The convergence of three independent tools on gentisic acid across iron-handling pathways and an aromatic-degradation KEGG entry reinforces the iron-homeostasis interpretation. Benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (KEGG:C14853) and the remaining five input compounds were not resolved to any pathway member in any tool output, suggesting they are either below annotation thresholds or function outside curated human pathway databases.

Across three independent paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA (Reactome namespace), Mummichog m/z-direct enrichment (human_mfn network), and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — the top convergent finding is Xenobiotics metabolism. In RaMP, REACT:R-HSA-211981 ranks 4th with FDR=0.0072 (coumarin as the sole hit, 1 of 52 pathway members), and its parent Reactome 'Xenobiotics' super-pathway (R-HSA-211897) for cytochrome P450 substrates is also significant at FDR=0.009. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA identifies KEGG:hsa00350 at rank 0 (p=0.052, gentisic acid hit), which encompasses aromatic xenobiotic catabolism. Coumarin (ChEBI:28794) is the primary driver: it is the sole input metabolite recovered in the xenobiotics pathway in both RaMP and Mummichog, and its InChIKey (ZYGHJZDHTFUPRJ) is structurally consistent across all compound references. Benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (BaP DE, ChEBI:30614) is the Phase I activation product of the carcinogen benzo[a]pyrene via cytochrome P450 enzymes — consistent with the RaMP cytochrome P450 pathway hit — placing it upstream of DNA-adduct formation. A secondary convergent signal is iron homeostasis: RaMP identifies 'Iron uptake and transport' (R-HSA-917937, FDR=0.007) and 'Metal sequestration by antimicrobial proteins' (R-HSA-6799990, FDR=0.006), both with gentisic acid (2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid, ChEBI:17189) as the hit, suggesting altered systemic iron handling. Mummichog independently recovers ubiquinone biosynthesis (rank 2, p=0.022), a pathway that requires iron as a cofactor for several enzymes. final_react_result.final_narrative_text: The differential metabolome is dominated by perturbation of xenobiotic metabolism. Across three independent paradigms — RaMP multi-DB ORA (Reactome namespace), Mummichog m/z-direct enrichment (human_mfn network), and MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA — the top convergent finding is Xenobiotics metabolism. In RaMP, REACT:R-HSA-211981 ranks 4th with FDR=0.0072 (coumarin as the sole hit, 1 of 52 pathway members), and its parent Reactome 'Xenobiotics' super-pathway (R-HSA-211897) for cytochrome P450 substrates is also significant at FDR=0.009. Mummichog independently recovers 'Xenobiotics metabolism' (MUMM:xenobiotics_metabolism) as its rank-0 hit (p=0.003) with two overlapping compounds. MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA identifies KEGG:hsa00350 at rank 0 (p=0.052, gentisic acid hit), which encompasses aromatic xenobiotic catabolism. Coumarin (ChEBI:28794) is the primary driver: it is the sole input metabolite recovered in the xenobiotics pathway in both RaMP and Mummichog, and its InChIKey (ZYGHJZDHTFUPRJ) is structurally consistent across all compound references. Benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (BaP DE, ChEBI:30614) is the Phase I activation product of the carcinogen benzo[a]pyrene via cytochrome P450 enzymes — consistent with the RaMP cytochrome P450 pathway hit — placing it upstream of DNA-adduct formation. A secondary convergent signal is iron homeostasis: RaMP identifies 'Iron uptake and transport' (R-HSA-917937, FDR=0.007) and 'Metal sequestration by antimicrobial proteins' (R-HSA-6799990, FDR=0.006), both with gentisic acid (2,5-dihydroxybenzoic acid, ChEBI:17189) as the hit, suggesting altered systemic iron handling. Mummichog independently recovers ubiquinone biosynthesis (rank 2, p=0.022), a pathway that requires iron as a cofactor for several enzymes. The metabolite set thus reflects a dual insult: xenobiotic Phase I/II processing stress (coumarin + BaP DE) and iron homeostasis perturbation (gentisic acid + elemental iron).
